description: What this shows: Peer connection quality: latency, divergence, version distribution and upgrade guidance, resource disconnects, and inbound/outbound balance.  —  Use it to: Assess how good this node's peer set is and whether connectivity or an upgrade needs attention.

panels.title: P90 Peer Latency
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*90th-percentile round-trip latency to connected peers, in milliseconds.*

###### How it's computed:
*Instantaneous gauge reading of the p90 peer latency.*

###### Reading it:
*Lower is better; green under 200ms, yellow to 500ms, red above.*

###### Healthy range:
*Under 200ms.*

###### Watch for:
*Rising latency, which points to network congestion or geographically distant, poorly performing peers.*

###### Keywords:
- **Peer** *(per node)* — another server this node holds a protocol connection to.
- **Overlay** *(network-wide)* — the peer-to-peer mesh xrpld nodes form to gossip transactions, proposals and validations.

###### Computation boundary:
*Result: Per node — each series is one server's own value.*
*Computed in xrpld code (MetricsRegistry, OpenTelemetry SDK) and exported as a metric; the collector only forwards it; the Grafana query selects and aggregates it.*

###### Source:
[AppMetricGauges.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/telemetry/AppMetricGauges.cpp)

###### Function:
`registerPeerQualityGauge`

###### References:
[Telemetry glossary](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/docs/telemetry-glossary.md#peer)

panels.title: Insane/Diverged Peers [$xrpl_network_type]
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*Count of connected peers whose ledger state has diverged from the network.*

###### How it's computed:
*Instantaneous gauge reading of the diverged-peer count.*

###### Reading it:
*Zero is healthy; any count means those peers disagree on ledger state.*

###### Healthy range:
*0 diverged peers.*

###### Watch for:
*A persistent non-zero count, which can indicate peers on a fork or misbehaving peers.*

###### Keywords:
- **Insane / diverged peers** *(per node)* — connected peers whose ledger state disagrees with the network — possibly on a fork or misbehaving.
- **Fork** *(network-wide)* — when nodes validate divergent ledger chains instead of a single agreed history.

###### Computation boundary:
*Result: Per node — each series is one server's own value.*
*Computed in xrpld code (MetricsRegistry, OpenTelemetry SDK) and exported as a metric; the collector only forwards it; the Grafana query selects and aggregates it.*

panels.title: Inbound vs Outbound Peers [$xrpl_network_type]
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*Active inbound versus outbound peer connection counts.*

###### How it's computed:
*Instantaneous gauge readings of active inbound and outbound peer counts.*

###### Reading it:
*A balanced mix is healthy for connectivity and resilience.*

###### Healthy range:
*A mix of both; some outbound connections present.*

###### Watch for:
*All-inbound with no outbound, which usually means NAT or firewall issues block outbound peering.*

###### Keywords:
- **Peer** *(per node)* — another server this node holds a protocol connection to.
- **Overlay** *(network-wide)* — the peer-to-peer mesh xrpld nodes form to gossip transactions, proposals and validations.

panels.title: Busiest Peer Share
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*The busiest peer's share of the validations this node receives, for trusted and for untrusted signers.*

###### How it's computed:
*The node counts the validations each peer delivers. At each collection it turns the counts into per-second rates and divides the busiest peer's rate by the total for that trust class. 0 when no validations arrived.*

###### Reading it:
*Near 1 means one peer carries almost all of that traffic. Traffic spread over many peers keeps it low.*

###### Healthy range:
*Well below 1 on a node with several peers.*

###### Watch for:
*An untrusted share near 1 during an untrusted validation flood: one peer carries it. Validation Load Warnings names that peer when it is over the per-peer limit.*

###### Keywords:
- **Peer** *(per node)* — another server this node holds a protocol connection to.
- **Trusted / untrusted** *(per node)* — a validation is trusted when its signer is on this node's UNL, untrusted otherwise.

###### Computation boundary:
*Result: Per node — each series is one server's own value.*
*Computed in xrpld code (AppMetricGauges, OpenTelemetry SDK) and exported as a metric; the collector only forwards it; the Grafana query selects it.*

###### Source:
[AppMetricGauges.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/telemetry/AppMetricGauges.cpp)

###### Function:
`registerPeerValidationLoadGauge`

###### References:
[Telemetry glossary](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/docs/telemetry-glossary.md#validation-load)

panels.title: Top-3 Peer Validation Rates
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*Validations per second from the three busiest peers, for trusted and for untrusted signers.*

###### How it's computed:
*The node counts the validations each peer delivers, including duplicates and untrusted ones it then drops. At each collection it turns the counts into per-second rates since the previous collection and reports the three highest for each trust class. A rank follows whichever peer was busiest in that interval, not one fixed peer.*

###### Reading it:
*Top 1 far above Top 2 and Top 3 means one peer sends most of the traffic. Lines close together mean the load is spread.*

###### Healthy range:
*Untrusted Top 1 under the per-peer warning limit, so Validation Load Warnings stays empty.*

###### Watch for:
*Untrusted Top 1 rising far above Top 2 during a flood: one peer carries it.*

###### Keywords:
- **Peer** *(per node)* — another server this node holds a protocol connection to.
- **Trusted / untrusted** *(per node)* — a validation is trusted when its signer is on this node's UNL, untrusted otherwise.

###### Computation boundary:
*Result: Per node — each series is one server's own value.*
*Computed in xrpld code (AppMetricGauges, OpenTelemetry SDK) and exported as a metric; the collector only forwards it; the Grafana query selects it.*

###### Source:
[AppMetricGauges.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/telemetry/AppMetricGauges.cpp)

`registerPeerValidationLoadGauge`

panels.title: Validation Load Warnings
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*Warning lines that name the busiest peer when its untrusted validation rate is over the per-peer limit.*

###### How it's computed:
*Raw log stream filtered to WRN lines that contain "Validation load: peer". Each line gives the peer's connection id, its node public key and its untrusted validations per second. The throttle is per connection: one connection is named at most once every five minutes, and a reconnect gets a new id.*

###### Reading it:
*Look the public key up in the peers admin command, which shows the peer's address while it is connected.*

###### Healthy range:
*Empty.*

###### Watch for:
*The same public key every few minutes: that peer keeps flooding this node.*

###### Keywords:
- **Log stream** *(per node)* — the raw lines behind the aggregate rates, newest first.

###### Computation boundary:
*Result: Raw log lines, no aggregation.*
*Rendered directly from Loki; no computation applied.*

###### Source:
[AppMetricGauges.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/telemetry/AppMetricGauges.cpp)

###### Function:
`registerPeerValidationLoadGauge`

###### References:
[Telemetry glossary](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/docs/telemetry-glossary.md#validation-load)

targets.expr: {service_name=~"$service_name", service_instance_id=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment"} |= `Validation load: peer` | xrpl_network_type =~ "$xrpl_network_type" | severity = `WRN` | line_format `{{.partition}}:{{.severity}} {{.message}}`

panels.title: Resource Disconnects
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*How many peers per minute this node drops for exceeding resource (load) limits.*

###### How it's computed:
*Per-minute rate of the resource-disconnect total over the rate interval. The total starts again from zero after a restart; the rate treats that as a restart, not a fall.*

###### Reading it:
*Zero is healthy; any line above zero means peers are being dropped for overuse.*

###### Healthy range:
*At or near zero.*

###### Watch for:
*A sustained non-zero rate, which flags aggressive or misbehaving peers being shed as backpressure.*

###### Keywords:
- **Resource disconnect** *(per node)* — a peer dropped for exceeding resource/load limits — the node shedding abusive or overactive peers.

###### Computation boundary:
*Result: Per node — each series is one server's own value.*
*Computed in xrpld code (MetricsRegistry, OpenTelemetry SDK) and exported as a metric; the collector only forwards it; the Grafana query selects and aggregates it.*

###### Source:
[AppMetricGauges.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/telemetry/AppMetricGauges.cpp)

`registerServerInfoGauge`
